To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the respiratory chain of nodulating bacteria is a complex and highly integrated process that is crucial for the symbiosis with the plant host, but that the specific features of the electron transport chain may vary among different species of nodulating bacteria.

(1) the respiratory chain is the main energy source for N2 fixation, and (2) the electron transfer chain is composed of two types of complex I, one of them (green complex I) is a new form of NADH dehydrogenase that may facilitate the energy metabolism of the nitrogenase complex.

(i) the efficiency of NADH dehydrogenase is a major determinant for N2 fixation; (ii) the efficiency of complex I depends on the presence of a proton-pumping NADH de-hydrogenase; and (iii) the presence of green complex I is a major determinant to increase the efficiency of NODULUS-RHIZOBIUM symbiosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the biochemistry and genetics of the symbiotic nitrogenase, and with the energy metabolism of the nodulating symbiont, with a view towards understanding the factors that limit the efficiency of biological N2 fixation in agriculture and in the natural environment.
the fundamental question of how bacteria can use energy to sustain the demanding process of N2 fixation and how this process can be improved for the benefit of agricultural productivity.
the fundamental question of the origin and function of the energy metabolism in the root nodule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we still have a poor understanding of the energy metabolism in nodules.
we still have to understand the fundamental aspects of the energy metabolism in the symbiosis between plants, bacteria and N2.
the efficiency of NADH oxidation and the capacity for N2 fixation are not correlated in the different symbiotic associations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the symbiotic bacteria have evolved to optimize the energy metabolism for the nitrogenase function.
, in the absence of a detailed understanding of the respiratory chain, it is impossible to fully comprehend the efficiency of the N2-fixing symbiosis.
the energy metabolism of N2-fixing bacteria in nodules is more diverse than expected, and the diversity is a reflection of the evolutionary history of these bacteria and the plants they infect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the respiratory chain is a limiting factor in N2 fixation.

the energy metabolism of the symbiotic bacteria is highly integrated with N2 fixation and that the symbiosis is a complex system that cannot be understood by studying the individual components in isolation.

a better understanding of the energy metabolism in nodules is required to improve the efficiency of Nodulation and Biological Nitrogen Fixation (NodBioN) and to facilitate the application of NodBioN in agriculture.
